questions.prompt: Sort each control by what it does.
questions.explain: Text in context advises. A prompt hands the decision to you. A deny rule or blocking hook refuses without consulting the model.

items.misconception: An instructions file is text the model reads. It cannot refuse a tool call.

items.text: A permission prompt before a push
items.misconception: The harness pauses and you decide. The choice sits with you.
A deny rule is applied by the harness whatever the model wants.
Exit 2 blocks the call, so it enforces.
Skill text enters the context as instructions, like any other advice.

questions.prompt: Which risk is the best fit for advice alone, such as a line in the instructions file?
questions.explain: Advice suits preferences where a miss costs a review comment. Anything that must never happen needs a control that does not depend on the model.

options.text: Using the project's variable naming style
Reading key files in the home directory
options.misconception: A leak cannot be undone, so it needs more than a request in text.

options.text: Running a destructive command on shared data
options.misconception: A destructive action calls for a rule, a hook or a sandbox; a polite request is advice.

options.text: Calling a server tool that deletes records
options.misconception: A tool call that deletes records needs a deny rule or a hook. Text only asks.

questions.prompt: A fetched web page contains text telling the agent to email your results elsewhere. Which response fits best?
questions.explain: Advice may not hold against text already in context, so limit what the agent can do: read-only servers, least privilege, deny rules, and a sceptical look at what was fetched.

options.text: Limit what the agent can do and read fetched content sceptically
Add a line to the instructions file saying to ignore web pages
options.misconception: That is advice, and advice may not hold against injected text.

options.text: Trust it, because the server was approved once
options.misconception: Approving a server leaves the content it fetches unverified.

options.text: Rely on the sandbox alone, since it stops every prompt injection
options.misconception: The sandbox limits shell commands and is off by default. It is one layer.

questions.prompt: A summary of the controls in this lesson has one wrong line. Which?
questions.explain: A hook that exits 0 with no JSON decision gives no decision, so the normal permission flow runs. Exit 2, or exit 0 with a JSON deny decision, blocks.

lines.text: A deny rule is applied by the harness, whatever the model wants
lines.why: Enforcement does not depend on the model's cooperation.

lines.text: A hook that exits 0 with no JSON decision blocks the tool call
Git history lets you recover after the fact
lines.why: A commit is a restore point.

lines.text: A project server in .mcp.json needs your approval in an interactive session
lines.why: Claude Code prompts before using project-scoped servers.

questions.prompt: Match each risk to the control that fits it best.
questions.explain: Pick the control by the cost of being wrong: advice for taste, a prompt for choices, enforcement for never.

pairs.misconception: Anything stronger costs more effort than a style miss is worth.

pairs.left: A push you want to approve each time
pairs.right: An ask rule or permission prompt
pairs.misconception: A deny rule would stop pushes you do want, and advice would not stop any.
Never means enforced by the harness, and a request to the model is advice.

pairs.left: A slip after the agent edits many files
pairs.misconception: Prevention failed by assumption here, so a restore point is what helps.

questions.prompt: A group wants an agent to stay under a monthly spend. Where should the cap live?
questions.explain: A budget the agent can exceed is not a limit. A cap in the system that meters the spend stops the action, while a line of instructions only asks.

options.text: In the metering system that counts the spend
In the instructions file, written as a clear rule
options.misconception: Instructions are advice. The model can drift from them, and nothing stops the spend.

options.text: In the opening prompt of every session
options.misconception: A prompt is still advice, and it can fall out of context in a long session.

options.text: In the agent's own running count of what it spent
options.misconception: The agent could miscount, and a limit the agent polices itself is not enforced.
